summary: Static rendered Deployment manifest snapshots make ADR-0199 tenant-cost-label coverage scan FD-001 backbone dogfood workloads with zero findings.
claim_boundary: This slice adds static rendered Deployment manifest snapshots generated from the current source Helm values/templates so the ADR-0199 tenant-cost-label advisory gate scans concrete FD-001 dogfood workload YAML. It does not claim Helm release rendering in CI, Kubernetes API admission, OpenCost allocation output, ArgoCD sync/health, branch-protection state, remote CI green, or production tenant workload deployment.

best_practice_research.used_for: Rendered snapshots preserve Kubernetes recommended app.kubernetes.io grouping labels plus Oyatie tenant/cost labels.
Rendered snapshots keep explicit resource requests/limits for future scheduler and cost/capacity accounting.
Rendered snapshots preserve liveness/readiness probe declarations.
Rendered snapshots preserve restricted-style security context posture already present in the source charts.
Grounded cost labels as future allocation dimensions while explicitly avoiding a live OpenCost report claim.

source_basis.use: The current advisory gate scans YAML files under microservices/*/iac/helm/**/rendered/*.yaml and counts missing required label keys.
The quality lane declares rendered Helm manifest coverage for ADR-0199 tenant cost labels.
The rendered snapshots mirror current source chart defaults and label/probe/resource/security structure.

findings: The follow-on is data-only plus CI smoke coverage: four rendered Deployment YAML snapshots, no new runtime code, no controller, and no dependency.
Selector labels remain minimal app labels; mutable tenant/cost/product labels live only on metadata and pod-template labels.
The tenant-cost-label advisory lane now observes four concrete FD-001 dogfood workload manifests instead of reporting an empty scan set.
Rendered snapshots make later admission, FinOps, and observability integration easier to validate without pretending a cluster or OpenCost pipeline is live.
Each rendered snapshot carries an explicit non-claim annotation to block accidental interpretation as applied cluster state.

CI governance smoke now treats rendered YAML as a distinct class and requires Deployment kind, probes, runtimeClassName, resources, securityContext, tenant/cost/regulatory labels, dogfood labels, and non-claim annotation.
The tenant-cost-label gate result moved from zero scanned manifests to four scanned manifests with zero findings, making empty-set false confidence less likely.
F3_adversarial.not_applicable_reason: This static rendered-manifest coverage slice is not a defect fix; adversarial coverage is the rendered YAML validation and existing tenant-cost-label gate result.
F3_adversarial.passing_fixture_id: tenant-cost-labels-coverage advisory scanned 4 manifests with 0 findings
F3_adversarial.diagnostic_asserted: Removing a required oya.io label from any rendered snapshot would produce a tenant-cost-labels-coverage finding or governance-smoke missing-key failure.

findings: Operators and future agents can inspect concrete workload YAML without mentally evaluating Helm placeholders.
The rendered snapshots parse as YAML and are included in both the advisory tenant-cost-label gate and backbone governance-smoke argument list.
Workflow path filters now include the rendered snapshot directories so future changes to these artifacts trigger backbone CI.

alternatives_named: Leave the ADR-0199 gate scanning zero manifests
Change the advisory gate to scan source Helm templates directly
Add static rendered snapshots under the gate's documented rendered path
F6_alternatives.selected_rationale: Adding static rendered snapshots uses the documented lane path, avoids broad gate semantics changes, and makes the empty-scan condition explicit without requiring cluster credentials.
rejected_reasons: Leaving zero scans preserves an avoidable false-confidence gap.
Scanning templates directly would blur the rendered-manifest lane contract and still not provide concrete YAML for downstream review.

findings: No secrets, credentials, tokens, certificate material, tenant records, network credentials, or cluster kubeconfig were added.
Rendered labels are low-cardinality static classification labels, not user data.
Snapshots preserve non-root pod security context, RuntimeDefault seccomp, dropped capabilities, and read-only root filesystem.
Static YAML snapshots have no runtime request-path performance impact.
Rendered snapshots supply future audit/FinOps classification evidence, but no compliance enforcement or cost allocation output is claimed.
Reverting removes four rendered YAML files, workflow path/smoke additions, and task/evidence text without touching selectors, service code, or live infrastructure.
Concrete pod-template labels create low-cardinality future correlation dimensions for logs, metrics, traces, and cost allocation.
No source chart selector changes or live Deployment upgrades are introduced.
Rendered snapshot paths use the existing iac/helm/**/rendered contract named in ADR-0199 coverage docs.
tasks/plan.md, tasks/todo.md, evidence, and audit-chain rows document rendered-snapshot scope and non-claims.
Static rendered outputs live under iac/helm/oyatie-cloud-dogfood/rendered while source Helm charts remain under iac/k8s/helm.
This is infrastructure evidence only; service domain, API, REST, persistence, broker, and worker boundaries are untouched.
No Cargo, npm, Helm, or provider dependency was added.
The rendered snapshot schema is standard apps/v1 Deployment YAML with explicit labels/probes/resources/securityContext.
Backbone CI path filters and governance smoke now cover the rendered snapshots; the repo-global tenant-cost-label advisory lane scans them as part of run-all.
